definitions.definition: ell=Int.toNat(λ). When λ≥0 its integer image is λ; this equality is used only under the stated nonnegativity hypothesis.
I={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin(n), of cardinal n. Index arithmetic in factorials and binomials is natural arithmetic; for each i∈I the scalar weight ell−2i uses integer subtraction before casting.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, X_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} x^r. Products of endomorphisms mean composition, rightmost factor first.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, Y_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂
definitions.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra generated by x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r, acting on V through the given representation; these actions are X_r and Y_r.
U=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K. K acts on the K factor. For any ℤ-endomorphism fU of M its induced operator on U sends mU⊗αU to fU(mU)⊗αU, for all mU∈M and αU∈K.

definitions.type: K-Lie algebra with its induced action on U
definitions.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K in the original Chevalley construction. Its action on U is induced from the lattice restrictions of x,y,h and extended K-linearly; the integral Chevalley lattice is used also in characteristic 2.
For j∈I, c_j=binom(ell,j). A bar over any integer or natural coefficient below means its image under ℤ→K.
Q=Y_ell X_ell. This is the operator called P in basis-proof.md; Q avoids conflict with the target ID P.

For i,j∈I, a_ij is the restriction of A_ij to M. Admissibility ensures that each divided-power factor preserves M and thus that this restriction exists. Superscript M on an operator denotes its restriction to M whenever preservation has been established. The existence and commutator formula for h^M are proved explicitly.
T=K⊗_ℤ M, with scalar action on the K factor.

definitions.type: scalar-extension operation on ℤ-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For f∈End_ℤ(M), hat(f)=LinearMap.baseChange K f∈End_K(T), the canonical scalar extension. Write x̂=hat(x^M), ŷ=hat(y^M), ĥ=hat(h^M), X̂_r=hat(X_r^M), Ŷ_r=hat(Y_r^M) when the lattice restrictions exist. The pure-tensor evaluation formula is established through the registered scalar-extension theorem.
F_ij=(c_j as a scalar in K)^{-1} hat(a_ij). Inversion uses the field's total inverse; nonzeroness of c_j is proved subsequently, not assumed in this definition.

inputs.statement: M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z (equivalently under every X_r,Y_r for r≥0). M is not assumed minimal.

U=M⊗_ℤ K is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-vector space of dimension n=ell+1>0. There exists a family G:I×I→End_K(U) with all of the following properties: for all i,j,k,l∈I, G_ij G_kl=G_il if j=k and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I}G_ii=Id_U; and every K-linear subspace W⊂U invariant under the original induced x,y actions is invariant under all G_ij. The induced h action is the commutator of the induced x and y actions. The representation is precisely the original L_K action, also in characteristic 2.

For every field F0, natural n0>0, finite-dimensional F0-vector space U0 with dimension n0, and family G0 of F0-linear endomorphisms indexed by 0≤i,j<n0, suppose G0_ij G0_kl=G0_il if j=k and zero otherwise and ∑_{0≤i<n0}G0_ii=Id_U0. Then every F0-linear subspace W0 of U0 invariant under all G0_ij equals zero or U0.

binders.type: family of F0-linear endomorphisms indexed by Fin(n0)×Fin(n0)

inputs.statement: The complex-linear Chevalley operators satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h; v≠0, xv=0, hv=λv.

output.statement: U=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace W⊂U invariant under the induced x,y,h actions equals zero or U; equivalently U is irreducible for the prescribed L_K action. Both λ=0 and p=2 are included, and K need not be algebraically closed.

locals.declaration: Choose the matrix-unit family G_U supplied by N004, including its invariance property.
Fix any K-linear subspace W of U.

argument.text: N004 supplies a nonzero finite-dimensional U of dimension n>0 and an I-indexed matrix-unit family; choose that family as G_U with its full asserted invariance property. Here I=Fin(n). These are the required hypotheses for the universal lemma N005 on the original tensor module U.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂U, and assume L1: W is invariant under the original induced x,y,h. Its invariance under x,y alone implies invariance under all G_U, by N004. Instantiate N005 with F0=K,n0=n,U0=U,G0=G_U,W0=W. S001 gives the dimension and matrix-unit hypotheses, so W=0 or W=U. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. Together with nonzeroness from N004 this proves the requested irreducibility. H005 and H006 ensure the lattice actions in L_K are defined; invariance under its generators is equivalent to invariance under their K-linear combinations, since W is a K-subspace.

All data remain arbitrary under the original hypotheses. H003 includes λ=0 and p=2; it imposes no algebraic-closure condition on K. The nonnegative integer conversion gives ell=0 when λ=0, so n=1 and N004 yields a nonzero one-dimensional module. When p=2 the permitted λ are 0 and 1, and N004 and N005 apply to both, with no distinct-weight condition in characteristic p. Hence neither boundary case is excluded by any step of this final implication.
